experiment: E1.4 antenna regimes and outdoor-to-indoor deployment, uplink and downlink, 3.5 vs 7.2 GHz
status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-11-07, committed before the first run; values, checks and tolerances are not changed after results are seen. AMENDED once after run 1 (see 'amendments'): class taxonomy completed, no value, threshold or tolerance changed

amendments.trigger: run 1 (code 7f3d402) failed check N8 in every case: K1-K4 do not cover all outcomes
amendments.diagnosis: every uncovered outcome lies in the sensitivity states indoor_low_indep / indoor_high_indep (F1: 211 + 950, F2: 1766 + 1565 of 48600 per state, all cases pooled); pattern: 7.2 GHz DL and UL feasible while the 3.5 GHz UL (and possibly DL) is not. With carrier-independent O2I variates, 7.2 GHz can be the better carrier on a realization, an outcome the E1.3 classes never needed. Zero uncovered outcomes in the four shared-variate states (and therefore in both mixes)
amendments.defect: pre-registration design: class list not exhaustive for the independent-variate sensitivity; not a code error
amendments.change: add class K6_7p2_both_without_3p5_both = 7.2 DL and 7.2 UL feasible and NOT (3.5 DL and 3.5 UL feasible); N8 now requires K1, K2, K3, K4, K6 to be mutually exclusive and exhaustive in every state AND K6 = 0 in the shared-variate states (strictly stronger; implied by the non-negative carrier offsets of N5)
amendments.unchanged: all parameters, thresholds, tolerances, states, mixes, draws and every other check; K1-K5 values are identical before and after the amendment

scope: same 27 links and 200 shadowing realizations as E1.2/E1.3 (geometry-conditioned TR 38.901 UMa, hash-checked inputs)
single user per carrier, no interference: SNR, not SINR; rate mapping, feasibility profiles F1/F2 and classes K1-K5 exactly as E1.3

antenna gains at link-budget level: element pattern, array gain and ideal steering toward the geometric UE direction (UPPER BOUND: no CSI error, no angular-spread loss; the realised gain in the TR 38.901 fast-fading channel is measured in E1.5)
three antenna regimes are reported separately and never pooled: A equal element count, B equal physical aperture, C deployment configuration from a cited source
deployment states (outdoor, in-car, indoor low-loss, indoor high-loss) are reported separately; the M.2412 mix is an exact weighted combination of the per-state results, not a random assignment
fractions are over 27 distance-stratified positions x 200 realizations, NOT area-weighted (E1c)

inputs.e13_reference: results/phase2/e1_3_link_budget/records.csv.gz and summary.json (E1.3; SHA-256 checked against its manifest), used only by check N3

gnb_sectors.serving_sector: the sector with the largest gain toward the UE (same sector at both carriers)

antenna_model.gnb_array: uniform planar array, rows x cols elements per polarisation, 0.5 wavelength spacing; one polarisation counted for gain; mechanical downtilt 0
antenna_model.gnb_gain: G = G_E,max + A_E(theta, phi - bearing) + 10 log10(rows * cols) + SAF_K(theta); SAF_K = normalised factor of a fixed K-element vertical subarray (TR 38.901 clause 7.3.1 weights), 0 dB when K = 1 (every element steerable)
antenna_model.steering: ideal steering of all TRX ports toward the geometric direction of the UE (upper bound)
antenna_model.same_gain_dl_ul: the gNB array gain toward the UE is identical in DL (transmit) and UL (receive): TDD, same array
antenna_model.ue_rx: n_rx isotropic (0 dBi) elements, maximum-ratio combining: +10 log10(n_rx) dB on the average DL SNR (upper bound)
antenna_model.ue_tx: uplink at a fixed UE e.i.r.p. of 23 dBm: no transmit-array gain is added (TS 38.101-1 power class 3 total power; Nokia 2024 Table 1 caps UE average e.i.r.p. at 23 dBm)
antenna_model.angles: TR 38.901 clause 7.1 GCS: zenith 90 deg = horizon, azimuth counter-clockwise from +x (scene x axis); UE direction from the gNB position of E1.1

o2i_model.source: TR 38.901 V16.1.0 clause 7.4.3 = ITU-R M.2412-0 Annex 1 section 3.2 model B (Table A1-8) and section 3.3
o2i_model.building: PL = PL_b(d3D-out + d3D-in) + PL_tw + 0.5 d2D-in + sigma_P x_P
o2i_model.pl_tw: 5 - 10 log10(sum p_i 10^(-L_i/10)); low-loss 0.3 standard glass + 0.7 concrete, sigma_P 4.4 dB; high-loss 0.7 IRR glass + 0.3 concrete, sigma_P 6.5 dB; L_glass = 2 + 0.2 f, L_IRR = 23 + 0.3 f, L_concrete = 5 + 4 f (f in GHz), Tables 7.4.3-1 and 7.4.3-2
o2i_model.d2d_in: min of two independent U(0, 25 m) draws (UMa), per link and realization; mean 8.333 m, median 7.322 m
o2i_model.o2i_shadowing: sigma_SF = 7 dB for O2I links (TR 38.901 Table 7.5-6 Part-1, UMa O2I column); independent of the outdoor E1.2 field (different link type, clause 7.6.3.4)
o2i_model.car: PL = PL_b + 9 + 5 x_car dB (clause 7.4.3.2); outdoor E1.2 loss and shadowing of the link
o2i_model.legacy_model_not_used: Table 7.4.3-3 (20 dB, single-frequency <6 GHz only) is not used: in a two-carrier study it would give 3.5 GHz a larger wall loss than 7.2 GHz
o2i_model.indoor_geometry: each outdoor position is the facade point: d2D-out = E1.1 2D distance and its geometric LOS state is the state of the outdoor part of the O2I link; the indoor UE lies d2D-in further along the horizontal gNB-UE direction on the ground floor (h_UT = 1.5 m); PL_b uses d2D = d2D-out + d2D-in and d3D = sqrt(d2D^2 + (h_BS - h_UT)^2) (TR 38.901 Figure 7.4.1-2); the gNB gain is evaluated toward the indoor UE
o2i_model.not_modelled: upper floors (M.2412: h_UT = 3(n_fl - 1) + 1.5, n_fl ~ U(1, N_fl), N_fl ~ U(4, 8)): the street-level LOS mask does not apply above the ground floor; ground floor is conservative for NLOS links (UMa NLOS loss falls by 0.6 dB per metre of UE height); deferred to E1c with building-resolved indoor positions
o2i_model.spatial_correlation: d2D-in, x_P, O2I shadowing and car loss are drawn independently per link: E1.4 reports only per-link marginal fractions, which do not depend on correlation between links

frequency_correlation.shared_states: outdoor, in_car, indoor_low, indoor_high: d2D-in, building type, x_P, O2I shadowing variate and x_car are the same at both carriers (TR 38.901 clause 7.6.5 treatment of the shadowing variate applied to all O2I variates)
frequency_correlation.independent_states: indoor_low_indep, indoor_high_indep: d2D-in and building type shared, x_P and the O2I shadowing variate drawn independently per carrier (sensitivity)

random.shape: (200 realizations, 27 links in E1.1 file order) each
random.common_random_numbers: the same draws are used by every case, so differences between cases are deterministic

deployment_states.outdoor: E1.2 outdoor loss unchanged (pedestrian reference; not part of the M.2412 mix)
deployment_states.indoor_low: O2I, low-loss building model, shared variates
deployment_states.indoor_high: O2I, high-loss building model, shared variates
deployment_states.indoor_low_indep: as indoor_low, x_P and O2I shadowing independent per carrier
deployment_states.indoor_high_indep: as indoor_high, x_P and O2I shadowing independent per carrier

M2412.source: ITU-R M.2412-0 Table 5(b) Dense Urban-eMBB: 80% indoor, 20% outdoor (in-car); 20% high-loss, 80% low-loss buildings

highloss50.source: 50% high-loss / 50% low-loss as used by Nokia 2024 (Table 1); outdoor share kept in-car

classes_added_by_amendment_1.K6_7p2_both_without_3p5_both: 7.2 DL and 7.2 UL feasible while 3.5 GHz is not feasible in both directions (possible only when 7.2 GHz is the better carrier on a link; expected only in the independent-variate sensitivity states)

thresholds_note: identical to configs/e1/e1_3_link_budget.json; F2 is normalised by the occupied bandwidth, so in case C the 200 MHz carrier needs twice the absolute UL rate of the 100 MHz carrier (stated with every C result)

R0_isotropic_e13.description: E1.3 main case (isotropic, 1 UE Rx) through the E1.4 pipeline: outdoor state must reproduce E1.3 exactly (check N3); other states give the pure O2I effect

A_equal_elements.description: equal element count: 8x16 per polarisation (8x16x2 = 256 elements, M.2412 maximum; Nokia 2024 3.5 GHz array) at both carriers; UE 4 Rx at both; M.2412 Configuration A powers, noise figures and 20 MHz

B_equal_aperture.description: equal gNB aperture: 8x16 at 3.5 GHz, 16x32 at 7.2 GHz (floor of 8 x 7.2/3.5 = 16.46 and 16 x 7.2/3.5 = 32.91; 4.00x the elements, 10 log10(4) = 6.02 dB vs the 6.27 dB path-loss gap); same conducted power, so 6.02 dB more e.i.r.p. at 7.2 GHz; UE unchanged (4 Rx); otherwise as A

C_deployment.description: Nokia 2024 Table 1 configuration: 3.5 GHz 100 MHz, 53 dBm, 8x16x2 (29 dBi), UE 4 Rx; 7 GHz (applied at 7.2 GHz) 200 MHz, 53 dBm, 16x32x2 (35 dBi), UE 8 Rx; UE e.i.r.p. 23 dBm; noise figures M.2412 Configuration A (not stated by the source)

S1_A_ue1rx.description: as A with a single UE receive element: isolates the gNB array from the UE receive gain

S2_C_7p2_43dbm.description: as C with 43 dBm at 7.2 GHz (Nokia 2024 second level: 78 dBm e.i.r.p. per 200 MHz = 75 dBm per 100 MHz)

S3_C_nlos_bf_loss.description: as C with the gNB gain reduced by 4.5 dB on links whose outdoor state is NLOS, at both carriers (Nokia 2024 Figure 1: 10 dBi measured in NLOS vs 14.5 dBi nominal); any frequency dependence of this loss is measured in E1.5, not assumed

S4_C_subarray.description: as C with the Nokia 2024 TRX architecture: each TRX feeds a fixed 4-element vertical subarray with 10 deg electrical downtilt (4:1 aggregation), ports steered ideally; creates elevation nulls near the site (first null at about 28 m for the 25.5 m height difference)

S5_A_sectors_rot60.description: as A with the three sectors rotated by 60 deg (bearings 90, 210, 330): the sector orientation of a single site is arbitrary

parameter_sources.element_and_sectors: SOURCED: TR 38.901 V16.1.0 Tables 7.3-1 and 7.8-1; element gain 8 dBi also ITU-R M.2412-0 Table 5(b) and Nokia 2024 Table 1
parameter_sources.array_3p5: SOURCED: Nokia 2024 Table 1 (8x16x2, 256 elements, 29 dBi); within ITU-R M.2412-0 Table 5(b) 'up to 256 Tx/Rx'
parameter_sources.array_7p2: ADAPTED: Nokia 2024 Table 1 7 GHz array (16x32x2, 1024 elements, 35 dBi) applied at 7.2 GHz; for regime B it is the equal-aperture array rounded down
parameter_sources.ue_rx_count: SOURCED for 3.5 GHz: TS 38.101-1 Rel-19 clause 7.2, minimum 4 Rx ports in n77/n78/n79 (and n104, 6425-7125 MHz); 4 Rx at 7.2 GHz in A/B is an ASSUMPTION adapted from n104; 8 Rx at 7 GHz in C from Nokia 2024 Table 1
parameter_sources.ue_eirp: SOURCED: 23 dBm (power class 3; Nokia 2024 Table 1 average UE e.i.r.p. 23 dBm)
parameter_sources.c_powers_bandwidths: SOURCED: Nokia 2024 Table 1 (53 dBm per 100 MHz at 3.5 GHz; 53 dBm or 43 dBm per 200 MHz at 7 GHz)
parameter_sources.c_7p2_n_prb: ASSUMPTION: 546 PRB at 30 kHz SCS (2 x 273, as two aggregated 100 MHz carriers); no 200 MHz FR1 channel exists in TS 38.101-1 Rel-19
parameter_sources.c_noise_figures: ASSUMPTION: ITU-R M.2412-0 Configuration A (5 / 7 dB) at both carriers; not stated by Nokia 2024
parameter_sources.o2i_and_car: SOURCED: TR 38.901 V16.1.0 clause 7.4.3, Tables 7.4.3-1, 7.4.3-2 and 7.5-6 (O2I sigma_SF 7 dB); ITU-R M.2412-0 Annex 1 sections 3.2-3.3
parameter_sources.deployment_mix: SOURCED: ITU-R M.2412-0 Table 5(b) Dense Urban-eMBB

checks.N1_identities: every record: rx = tx + direction gain - loss; noise = -174 + 10 log10(B) + NF; SNR = rx - noise (abs error <= 1e-9 dB)
checks.N2_reciprocity: for every case, state, link, realization and carrier: DL and UL use the same total loss and the same gNB gain (abs error <= 1e-9 dB)
checks.N3_e13_reproduction: R0 outdoor reproduces the E1.3 main_eqbw20 records (DL SNR, UL best-allocation SNR, UL 1-PRB SNR: abs error <= 1e-9 dB; rates: abs error <= 1e-6 bit/s; F1/F2 flags identical) and its K1-K5 fractions exactly
checks.N4_gain_bounds: every gNB gain is finite and <= G_E,max + 10 log10(rows * cols) (+1e-12); the serving sector is identical at both carriers
checks.N5_carrier_offsets: states outdoor, in_car, indoor_low, indoor_high: SNR(3.5) - SNR(7.2) equals the analytic offset from the case parameters, for DL (full band) and UL (1 PRB), every record (abs error <= 1e-9 dB); analytic DL offset = dP_gNB - 10 log10(B1/B2) - dNF_UE + dG_nominal + 10 log10(n_rx1/n_rx2) + 20 log10(f2/f1) + [PL_tw(f2) - PL_tw(f1)]; UL offset = dP_UE - 10 log10(PRB1/PRB2) - dNF_gNB + dG_nominal + 20 log10(f2/f1) + [PL_tw(f2) - PL_tw(f1)]
checks.N6_o2i_components: PL_tw used equals an independent re-evaluation of Table 7.4.3-2 (abs error <= 1e-9 dB); PL_in = 0.5 d2D-in; 0 <= d2D-in <= 25 m; shared variates identical across carriers in shared states and different in independent states
checks.N7_draw_statistics: n = 5400 per variate: d2D-in mean within 4 x 5.8926/sqrt(n) of 8.3333 m and std within 4/sqrt(2n) (relative) of 5.8926 m; each standard-normal variate: |mean| <= 4/sqrt(n) and |std - 1| <= 4/sqrt(2n)
checks.N8_partition_and_mix: AMENDMENT 1: K1, K2, K3, K4 and K6 are mutually exclusive and cover every outcome of every case, state and profile, and K6 = 0 in the shared-variate states; mix weights are non-negative and sum to 1 (original text: 'K1-K4 cover every outcome of every case, state and profile')
checks.N9_mapping: as E1.3 L5 (mapped SE <= Shannon; 0 below -10 dB; <= Thr_max; non-decreasing)
checks.N10_ul_allocation: as E1.3 L6 (uplink maximum rate >= rate at 1 PRB and at full allocation)
checks.L8_unit_tests: unit tests reproduce hand-computed element, subarray and O2I values (tests/test_antenna.py, tests/test_o2i.py)

expectations_stated_before_run.note: analytic consequences of the model, stated before the run; they are hypotheses to report, not pass criteria (except where also a check)

carrier_offset_db.S2_C_7p2_43dbm: DL offsets of C + 10 dB; UL offsets as C

expectations_stated_before_run.dl_minus_ul_fullband_db: R0 and S1: 19.00; A and B: 25.02 (UE 4 Rx adds 6.02 dB to DL only); C: 34.02 at 3.5 GHz and 37.03 at 7.2 GHz
predictions: A: the K2 loss window keeps its E1.3 width (6.27 dB outdoor); array gain moves links from K3/K4 toward K1
B and C: outdoor K2 almost vanishes (window 0.24 dB); indoor high-loss reopens it to about 4.9 dB because wall loss grows with frequency
UE 4 Rx raises DL only, so A has more 'DL works, UL fails' outcomes than S1
indoor states shift every class toward K3/K4; high-loss buildings dominate the M.2412-mix K4 fraction
